_comment: Golden set for ranking evals. Authored (not scraped), license-clean, deterministic. Items are FeedItem-shaped; profiles carry graded relevance labels (2 = highly relevant, 1 = related; ids absent from a profile are off-topic = 0). Topics are deliberately discriminating so a good ranker clearly beats a bad one, and each profile hides one semantically-relevant item that shares no topic words with the profile — the lexical ranker misses it, leaving measurable headroom for the Inc 3 embedding ranker.

items.title: Fine-tuning an LLM for your own domain
items.content: Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model with a small labelled set. We walk through data prep, LoRA adapters, and evaluation — a practical machine learning workflow for shipping a domain LLM.

items.title: How transformers power modern neural networks
items.content: Attention lets a model weigh every token against the others. This piece unpacks why transformers replaced recurrent neural networks for most sequence tasks in modern AI.

items.title: Running quantized neural networks at the edge
items.content: Quantization shrinks a trained model so it runs on constrained devices with tight latency budgets. We benchmark accuracy loss across int8 and int4 for on-device machine learning.

items.title: Evaluating model output with graded rubrics
items.content: Good evals grade an LLM's answers on a rubric instead of exact match. Machine learning teams use graded relevance to catch quality regressions before users do.

items.title: Reinforcement feedback and reward models
items.content: RLHF trains a reward model from human preferences, then optimises a policy against it — a machine learning loop now standard for aligning transformers.

items.title: Container queries land in every major browser
items.content: Container queries let a component respond to its own size, not the viewport. Shipping in every browser makes truly modular CSS layouts practical on the web platform.

items.title: WebAssembly brings native speed to the browser
items.content: WebAssembly runs compiled code at near-native speed inside the browser sandbox, opening the web platform to games, codecs, and heavy compute.

items.title: Structured concurrency arrives in JavaScript
items.content: Structured concurrency ties async tasks to a scope so nothing leaks. The proposal brings clearer cancellation to JavaScript running in the browser.

items.title: View Transitions for smoother navigation
items.content: The View Transitions API animates between states with a few lines. It works in every modern browser and uses CSS for the animation.

items.title: Building a scalable design system
items.content: A design system pays off when tokens and components share one source of truth. Modern CSS variables make theming across the web platform straightforward.

items.title: A critical vulnerability in a popular auth library
items.content: The flaw let an attacker bypass authentication entirely. Patch now; the security advisory rates it critical and a proof-of-concept exploit is already public.

items.title: Rotating encryption keys without downtime
items.content: Envelope encryption lets you re-wrap data keys without re-encrypting everything. A clean rotation story is table stakes for any serious security team.

items.title: Passkeys and the future of authentication
items.content: Passkeys replace passwords with device-bound credentials, killing phishing at the root. It is the biggest authentication shift in a decade for security teams.

items.title: Anatomy of a supply-chain attack
items.content: A single poisoned dependency became a working exploit against thousands of apps — a reminder that a transitive vulnerability is still your security problem.

items.title: End-to-end privacy for group messaging
items.content: End-to-end encryption keeps a group chat readable only to its members. Getting the security model right for large groups is surprisingly hard.

items.title: A new GPU architecture built for inference
items.content: The chip trades general-purpose flexibility for dense matrix throughput; the purpose-built hardware and its silicon are tuned end-to-end for low-latency inference.

items.title: The RISC-V processor gains real momentum
items.content: An open instruction set means anyone can design a processor without licensing fees. Foundries are taping out RISC-V silicon in real volume.

items.title: Inside a modern memory controller chip
items.content: The controller is the traffic cop between cores and DRAM. This chip devotes real silicon and careful hardware design to scheduling.

items.title: Why chiplets are the future
items.content: Splitting a design into chiplets lets each chip use the best process node. It is how modern silicon keeps scaling as monolithic dies hit the reticle limit.

items.title: Power efficiency in mobile devices
items.content: Battery life is won in the processor. Low-leakage silicon lets a mobile chip sip power without throttling under sustained load.

items.title: A faster build system for large monorepos
items.content: Content-addressed caching means you rebuild only what changed. For a big monorepo the right build tools turn a coffee break into a few seconds.

items.title: Debugging async code without losing your mind
items.content: Async bugs hide across await points where stack traces go quiet. Good developer tooling reconstructs the causal chain so debugging feels linear again.

items.title: Writing a compiler plugin in an afternoon
items.content: Modern compiler APIs expose the AST so you can add a lint or codemod cheaply. We build a small plugin and wire it into the developer workflow.

items.title: Modern terminal utilities that speed you up
items.content: A new wave of CLI tools — fuzzy finders, better greps, smarter pagers — makes the developer's day faster without ever leaving the terminal.

items.title: Reproducible environments with containers
items.content: Pin every dependency so a new machine reproduces your setup byte for byte — reproducible builds give a developer team auditable, tamper-evident releases.

items.title: Designing onboarding that users actually finish
items.content: Great onboarding respects the reader's time and removes every step that is not essential to the first win.

items.title: How to say no to a feature request
items.content: A focused roadmap means turning down good ideas so the few that matter ship well and on time.

items.title: Pricing your subscription without guesswork
items.content: Value-based pricing beats cost-plus for most subscription products; anchor on the outcome the reader buys, not the cost to serve.

items.title: Roadmaps that survive contact with reality
items.content: Outcome-oriented roadmaps flex as you learn from real usage instead of committing to fixed dates a year out.

items.title: Measuring activation, not just signups
items.content: Activation — the first real moment of value — predicts retention far better than raw signup counts ever will.
